**Lines 46-50, 106-112, 115, 144-149, 156-162, 170-175**

The `Get` fast path, `Set`, `Refresh`, `LoadOrStore`, and `cleanup` all read/write `c.data` without holding the mutex.

Goroutine B: Set() writes c.data[key] = ... (line 106)

## The Corrected Fate

```go
func (c *Cache) Get(ctx context.Context, key string) (interface{}, error) {
    c.mu.Lock()
    entry, ok := c.data[key]
    if ok && time.Now().Before(entry.ExpiresAt) && !entry.Loading {
        c.mu.Unlock()
        atomic.AddInt64(&c.stats.Hits, 1)
        return entry.Value, nil
    }
    // ... hold lock through loading decision, use sync.Cond for waiters
}

func (c *Cache) Set(key string, value interface{}) {
    c.mu.Lock()
    defer c.mu.Unlock()
    c.data[key] = &CacheEntry{...}
}

func (c *Cache) GetMulti(ctx context.Context, keys []string) map[string]interface{} {
    var wg sync.WaitGroup
    var mu sync.Mutex
    results := make(map[string]interface{})
    for _, key := range keys {
        wg.Add(1)
        go func(k string) {
            defer wg.Done()
            if v, err := c.Get(ctx, k); err == nil {
                mu.Lock()
                results[k] = v
                mu.Unlock()
            }
        }(key)
    }
    wg.Wait()
    return results
}
```

Use `sync.RWMutex` for read-heavy paths. Use `atomic` for stats. Use `sync.Cond` instead of busy-wait. Hold lock across load-store to prevent lost invalidations, or use versioning.
